title: Social Sciences · Seq 2 Social sciences and their disciplines

options: The term comes from the Greek anthropos (mankind) and logos (study)
It is also a natural science in some respects
It is limited to the study of "primitive" societies
It is the comparative study of humans as a group
questions.explanation: Being limited to primitive societies is listed as a misconception.

questions.stem: The four main sub-fields of anthropology are:
options: Physical anthropology
Sociocultural anthropology
Linguistic and archaeological anthropology
Applied anthropology, the best-established branch
questions.explanation: Applied anthropology is sometimes added as a fifth branch but is not as well established.

options: Natural features studied by physical geography
The material remains of human societies
The footprints on the ecology left by past societies
Written records of ancient societies
questions.explanation: Artifacts = material remains; ecofacts = ecological footprints of past societies.

options: Studies language as a cultural resource and speaking as a cultural practice
Usually focuses on unwritten languages
Studies only the grammar of written Western languages
Is also called anthropological linguistics or ethnolinguistics
questions.explanation: Duranti (1997). It often studies languages of indigenous non-Western peoples with no form of writing.

questions.stem: Misconceptions about anthropology listed in the course:
options: Anthropologists only study rural people and rural areas
Anthropology overlaps with other disciplines that study society
Anthropology is limited to "primitive" societies
Anthropologists want to preserve defunct cultural practices in museums
questions.explanation: Overlap with other disciplines (law, religion, politics, art…) is true, not a misconception.

options: Herodotus is called the father of history
Ibn Khaldun is called the father of historiography
The word comes from the Greek Historie, meaning careful enquiry or investigation
Historiography is the study of the earth's surface
questions.explanation: Historiography = the writing of history based on critical examination of sources.

questions.stem: According to the course, the fruits of the study of history are:
options: Exact laws of human behaviour
Appreciation of variety
Imposition of order
Possibilities of prediction and realization of limitation
questions.explanation: Four fruits: order, variety, prediction, limitation.

options: It starts with the first artefacts, about 2.5 million years ago in East Africa
Ethno-archaeologists study how people living today organize and use objects
The word means "discourse about ancient things"
Prehistoric archaeologists study the period after the Industrial Revolution
questions.explanation: Prehistoric = before writing; industrial archaeologists study the post-Industrial-Revolution period.

options: Geography also studies humans
Geography is limited to map-making
Geology studies the human landscape
Geology focuses mainly on the physical Earth and the processes shaping it
questions.explanation: Geography = natural environment and its influence on social and cultural development (Dorrell et al., 2019).

questions.stem: The two main divisions of geography and the link between geography and other disciplines:
options: The link is the spatial perspective
The link is the chronological perspective
Human geography — the human landscape and human–environment relations
Physical geography — physical features of the earth
questions.explanation: "If a phenomenon can be mapped, it has some kind of relationship to geography."

options: "Political" comes from the Greek polis (city or sovereign state)
Government is the only institution with legitimate authority to use coercive power
Aristotle viewed man as a "political animal"
Its main subfield is microeconomics
questions.explanation: Subfields: political theory, comparative politics, international relations, political economy, political sociology, public administration, environmental politics.

options: Adam Smith is known as the father of modern economics
The word comes from oikos and nemein: "one who manages a household"
Karl Marx promoted the self-regulating economy
Alfred Marshall saw economics as a study of wealth and a study of man
questions.explanation: Marx challenged capitalism with the labour theory of value; Smith, Rousseau and Locke promoted the self-regulating economy.

options: Has price determination as its central problem
Deals with partial equilibrium analysis
Studies individual economic units
Is also called aggregative economics
questions.explanation: Macroeconomics = aggregative economics, general equilibrium, level of income and employment.

options: Poverty and unemployment are the biggest problems in Africa
The life expectancy at birth in Somalia is rising
The poor should pay no taxes
Females ought to be given job opportunities
questions.explanation: Normative = value judgments ("what ought to be"). C and D are the course's examples of positive economics.

questions.stem: Match the psychologist to the approach:
options: Sigmund Freud — psychoanalytic theory
Abraham Maslow — behaviourism
William James — functionalism
Wundt — structuralism
questions.explanation: Maslow (with Carl Rogers) is humanistic psychology. Skinner is the behaviourist.

options: Spoke of reinforcement and punishment as major factors driving behaviour
Introduced Gestalt principles in the United States
Was a behaviourist
Developed the operant conditioning chamber
questions.explanation: Gestalt principles were introduced by Wertheimer, Koffka and Köhler.

questions.stem: The word Gestalt roughly translates to:
options: Mind
Whole
Structure
Behaviour
questions.explanation: Gestalt psychology: how parts relate to each other as a whole in perception.

options: The term was coined by Auguste Comte in 1838
The first US sociology course was taught at Harvard in 1950
The first European department was founded in Bordeaux in 1895 by Durkheim
It comes from the Latin socius (companion) and the Greek logos
questions.explanation: First US course: University of Kansas, 1890 (Elements of Sociology).

questions.stem: A study of the accepted rules of conversation among teenagers is an example of:
options: Macro-level sociology
Archaeological anthropology
Normative economics
Micro-level sociology
questions.explanation: Macro-level analysis looks at trends among large groups, e.g. how language use has changed over time.

questions.stem: About Ibn Khaldun's New Science ('Ilm al-'Umran):
options: Its central concept is 'Assabiyya — what holds groups together
It holds that social phenomena are the outcome of chance
It uses a dualist bedouin/sedentary typology
Its introduction is the Muqaddimah ("Prologue")
questions.explanation: He stressed that social and historical phenomena are controlled by laws that must be discovered.

questions.stem: According to Ibn Khaldun, historians commit errors because of:
options: Bias and prejudice
Blind acceptance of reports given by others
Excessive use of statistics
Ignorance of the natures of civilization and peoples
questions.explanation: Three major factors; remedies include absolute objectivity and checking reports and reporters.
